details: CalculiX dynamic contact output parsed for activation, penetration, force, contact energy, and contact-zone stress
Uses loose diagnostic thresholds; false means evidence exists but external contact agreement is not accepted
Replays SFC hard-linear area-weighted contact law on CalculiX displacements to separate force-law/output differences from trajectory differences
Checks the HHT residual evaluation point, previous static residual update, and contact residual tangent sign convention by finite differences
Tracks CNUM lifecycle transitions, RF/CELS peak timing, and source-level output definitions for CalculiX/SFC contact comparison
Tracks CalculiX DIRECT increment attempts, Newton iterations, convergence messages, HHT alpha/beta/gamma, and SFC Newton acceptance diagnostics
Starts SFC from each CalculiX displacement state and decomposes internal force, contact force, mass term, HHT residual, tangent norms, and Newmark update error
Checks CalculiX beta/gamma, prediction/update/residual state definitions, initial acceleration regularization, mass scale, and .dat displacement precision amplification
Parses per-contact CDIS/CSTR/CELS from CalculiX .dat and compares CalculiX active contact elements against SFC native and CalculiX-displacement replay springs
Requests and parses CalculiX nodal V/A output to avoid relying only on displacement-differenced Newmark acceleration reconstruction
Requests floor nodal RF without totals-only aggregation and sums it separately for reaction-force diagnostics
Preserves every CDIS/CSTR/CELS data row with raw row index instead of overwriting or face-aggregating repeated contact-element rows
Compares clearance, area, force, energy, normal, and slave weights at the nominal first contact step
Directly compares CalculiX printed nodal velocity V against SFC nodal velocity at matching output times
r1/r2/r3 SFC geometric contact trend; no theoretical order claimed
dt, dt/2, dt/4 SFC geometric contact trend
SFC and CalculiX final VTK stress clouds are written with shared von Mises color scale fields
